W.C.S. OF THE METHODIST CHURCH

Holds Regular Meeting

Harriettsville, June 18— Mrs. C. E. Johanning entertained the W.C.S. of the Methodist church at her home Thursday evening. Mrs. Johanning led the devotionals. After the business meeting a social hour was enjoyed and the church hymn books were repaired.

Refreshments of chicken sandwiches, pickles, cake, fruit salad and coffee were served to the following: Mrs. H. M. Ayers, Mrs. G. B. Johanning, Mrs. G. E. McVay, Mrs. Glen Wilson, Mrs. Alfred Mantel, Mrs. A. C. Kelby, Mrs. John Haffner, Mrs. L. D. Schramm, Misses Nina Lee Hendershot, Dora Jane and Mary Mallett, Donna Lee, Virginia Lee, Ellen Heisler, Faye and Hazel Schafer, Beulah Mantel, Norma Jean Williams, Ann and Aundree Johanning, Mary Ellen Wilson, Billie Mallett, Daniel Schramm, Raphael Williams, Roger Hendershot, and Gary Wilson.

The July meeting will be held at the home of Mrs. L. D. Schramm.

Huffman Lad Injured

Bobbie Huffman, four year old son of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Huffman suffered a fractured leg Saturday at Marietta where he was struck by truck while crossing the street. He was taken to the office of DR. Williams where the fracture was examined.

Dinner Guests

Dinner guests of Mrs. Barbara Wooster, Wednesday, were Mrs. Lizzie Roger of Robin, Mrs. Hazel Knight, Mrs. Luretta Reynolds and Mrs. Fanchion Wetzler of Byesville.

Attend Cousins Wedding

Miss Ada Ayers and Supt. and Mrs. H. M. Ayers and son, David attended the church wedding of their cousin, Roy Ayers, son of Mr. and Mrs. Ed. Ayers, of Alliance and Miss Norma Jean Braucher, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Russell H. Braucher, of Canton, Saturday evening, June 14, and the reception which followed.

Returned Home

Miss Martha Ullman was removed to her home Sunday from Marietta Memorial hospital, where she underwent surgery, Wednesday, June 11, and is recovering nicely. Miss Ullman has just completed her junior year at Muskingum college and is spending her summer vacation at her home here.

Underwent Surgery

Miss Justine Smithberger underwent surgery at Marietta Memorial hospital, Monday, June 9.

Fathers Day Dinner

Mr. and Mrs. G. E. Johanning entertained with a family dinner Sunday, honoring Fathers Day and their daughter, Mrs. Fanchion Rawlette, of Alexandria, Va. Those present were Mr. and Mrs. L. D. Schramm and son, Daniel; Mr. and Mrs. Henry Schenk and Mr. and Mrs. C. B. Johanning and children, Ann and Aundree.

Many Attend Love Funeral

Among those from a distance attending the funeral of Clark Love, Wednesday, were Mrs. Jane Sloan and daughter, Minnie, of Marietta; Mr. and Mrs. Willard Love and family of Woodsfield; Mr. and Mrs. Nelson Miller; Mr. and Mrs. Eugene Miller; Mae Miller; Mr. and Mrs. Frank Bonar and family; and Herman Smith of Columbus, and Mrs. Alta Killer of Marietta.

Children's Day Program

The Children's Day program held Sunday at the Methodist church was largely attended and an appropriate program was given. The special services opened by singing "Once Again the Morning Bell Are Ringing"; responsive reading by the group; prayer by Mrs. Velma Kelby; recitation by Faye Cunningham; song, "Beautiful June"; short play by Norma Williams and four children, "Giving Thanks"; recitation by Daniel Schramm; song, "Out in the Fields with God"; play, "Life's Weavers" by Chester Lee, Beulah Mantel and Faye Schafer; songs, "I Can Help" and "What One Little Boy Did" by Ellen Heisler; song, "Such is the Kingdom" by Ellen Wilson; song, "Queen of the Season"; recitation, "Child in the Garden" by Nina Lee Henderson; during the offering, Ellen Heisler presided at the piano; song, "In the Garden of Summer Time"; recitation by Hazel Ann Schafer, "Goodbye to Children's Day." The program concluded with the group singing "God Be With You Til We Meet Again."

Golden Wedding Anniversary

Mr. and Mrs. Edward Killer of Lower Salem route celebrated their golden wedding anniversary Sunday, June 15. Open house was held from 2 to 5 o'clock. Dinner was served to the children, grandchildren and close relatives.

Attend Judging Contest

L. D. Schramm and Carlo Miller accompanied group to Chester, W. Va., to attend a field day on the W. C. Smith 5000 acre farm. A judging contest of purebred Hereford cattle was held. Mr. Smith has 600 head of such cattle.

GREENSBORO, Dec. 7. W.
Federal Judge Johnson HAYNES took under advisement TODAY a motion by the Amazon Cotton Mills of Thomasville, to dismiss a petition by the Textile Workers Union (CIO) for an injunction restraining the mills from alleged refusal to bargain collectively with the union and also a $50,000 damage suit brought by the union;

Attorneys for the TWUA and the cotton mills, scene of a lengthy strike, argued for two and a half hours on the matter;

Judge Haynes said it would take him several days to reach decision. If the motion for dismissal is denied, he added, he will then hear evidence in the suit.

A company forbidding mass picketing at the Amazon plant was not mentioned at today's proceedings.

Superior Judge Hoyle Sink issued a restraining order in state court originally but the union sought its transfer to federal court. The district court clerks of Lee said that so far it has not received the papers in the case.

Urging dismissal of the TWUA's proceedings, company attorneys argued that the union had no legal right to sue, that the district court was without jurisdiction, and that the bill of complaint stated no grounds for the granting of relief.

In contradiction, the union lawyers contended that the Taft-Hartley law specifically gave the labor organization the right to sue, either as an entity or on behalf of individuals, and that the district court is given jurisdiction concurrently with the National Labor Relations Board in matters involving alleged unfair labor practices. Specifically they added the union had charged the company with failure to bargain collectively and had asked the injunction to compel the management to negotiate with representatives of the employees.
